issues.body: The added Anthropic test requires `[opus5, fable, opus, sonnet, haiku]`, while `orchestration/routing.toml` states that `fable` and `opus` were removed and that `opus5` is the sole Anthropic tier (with sonnet/haiku retained only for their limited routes). Extra account capability aliases do not create a route or weaken allocation checks, so this does not make the worker-cap fix unsafe, but the test's claim that it mirrors the catalog is inaccurate and will actively prevent the mint defaults from being cleaned up to match current routing policy.
issues.fix_hint: Derive or assert the Anthropic mint list against the current supported routing catalog, or explicitly document and test why account capability metadata intentionally remains a superset of dispatchable aliases. Avoid pinning retired aliases as a required invariant without that policy.
issues.title: New exact default assertion pins aliases removed from the routing catalog

verdict.summary: The workflow now derives the per-provider worker cap alongside the existing model metadata, transports it through a step output, rejects a missing value before persistence, and writes the derived value into the schema-validated account record. The new self-tests execute the real derivation for both providers, validate the resulting records through the real allocator parser, and check the register-step transport and consumption, so the core regression coverage is non-vacuous. One non-blocking inconsistency remains: the new exact Anthropic expectation preserves aliases that the current routing catalog declares removed.
